name: Blue Heart
tldr: 💙 usually shows friendship or team loyalty; in a baby announcement, it can mean the baby is a boy.

contextMeanings.meaning: At its most basic, 💙 stands for a blue heart or the color blue.
contextMeanings.example: the main color for this design is 💙

contextMeanings.meaning: Between close friends, 💙 often expresses affection without carrying a romantic charge.
In a sarcastic sports comment, 💙 can claim support for a team while implying that the team is doing badly.
In an early dating conversation, 💙 can show friendly approval without making a clear romantic confession.
contextMeanings.example: we have the same terrible taste in movies 💙

contextMeanings.meaning: In a work thread, 💙 can convey friendly appreciation or team solidarity, although it may be too vague to count as formal approval.
contextMeanings.example: love where this project is heading 💙

platformNotes.note: In a private iMessage thread, 💙 can close a warm conversation between friends without sounding like a romantic declaration. The surrounding relationship usually makes the intended affection clear.
On Instagram, 💙 appears in captions for team loyalty, friendship, and baby announcements. In a public post, the surrounding caption matters because strangers may not know which meaning you intend.
In TikTok comments, 💙 is often a quick way to support a creator or signal allegiance to a team. It works best as a reaction to the specific post rather than as a stand-alone comment with no context.

On WhatsApp, 💙 can be affectionate in family and friend groups, including the boy announcement in a baby reveal. A bare heart in a serious conversation may still leave recipients unsure whether it is affection, team support, or just a color.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z users often place 💙 within the wider use of colored hearts for platonic affection, so it may read as a friend-to-friend love you rather than a confession.
Millennials may use 💙 for team loyalty as readily as friendship, especially when a sports game or club supplies the context.
Unlike the pink heart, 💙 has no comparably strong generational split in the guide's examples. It can therefore land on friendship or team support when the conversation makes that clear.
A boomer may not automatically assign 💙 the friendship or team meaning that younger friends expect. Plain words such as love you, friend, or I support them can prevent confusion.

warnings.title: Baby reveal mistaken for a girl
warnings.description: In a pregnancy announcement, 💙 commonly identifies the baby as a boy. If the reveal is meant to remain a surprise, use 👶🎀 or say that the details are being withheld.

warnings.title: Friendship mistaken for flirting
warnings.description: A male friend may use 💙 for same-sex friendship without any romantic intent, while the recipient could still read it as a confession. Add clear wording such as you're one of my closest friends 💙 if the relationship could be uncertain.

seoDescription: What does 💙 mean? It usually shows friendship or loyalty to a team, while in a baby announcement it can announce that the baby is a boy.

longForm.overview:
💙 began as a blue heart when Unicode added it in 2010. At first, the glyph was simply the color blue in a heart shape; it did not carry a settled social meaning. Once hearts became a larger emoji palette, blue settled into two common jobs: showing friendship without romantic charge, and marking loyalty to a team. That makes love you 💙 from a male friend read as same-sex friendship, while a 💙 under a sports post says the sender supports that side.

The color is not a universal code for romance. Among early friends, it can do the light I like you beat without moving the relationship forward. In a pregnancy announcement, though, blue may mean that the baby is a boy. That last use is specific to a gender-reveal context, not a general meaning attached to blue. The important difference is the surrounding conversation: friendship, sports, and a baby reveal each give 💙 a different job.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
💙 is common in close friend threads, where love you 💙 can be a male friend saying he values the friendship without turning it into a romantic message. It also works as a sign-off after a good conversation, with no explanation needed once both people know the heart means friendship.

In sports conversations, the sender uses it to declare support for a club or team. A reply like 💙🔥 is enough to say I’m on your side. In a baby announcement, the same glyph moves into a completely different job: a blue heart can identify the baby as a boy.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Don’t use 💙 as your only opening in a dating app if you want the romantic meaning to be unmistakable. It can function as a friendly I like you gesture in an early friendship, so state your interest in words when that distinction matters. Hey, I like you 💙 is clearer than leaving the heart to make the confession.

Likewise, don’t use blue for a baby reveal unless you mean a boy; use 👶🎀 for a reveal that should remain open to surprise. In a work channel, a bare 💙 may be too ambiguous to count as approval, so say nice work alongside it. The main mistake is assuming blue always carries one fixed feeling.
longForm.howToReply:
If a friend sends love you 💙, replying with 💙 keeps the exchange friendly and low-key. Avoid automatically switching to ❤️, though: in a thread that has used blue or white hearts, red can look like the sender is deliberately increasing the romantic temperature. A sentence such as same, you’re one of my favorite people makes the affection clearer.

If the heart accompanies a sports post, mirror it or add the team emoji to show shared loyalty. For a baby announcement, congratulate them and use boy 💙 if you want to make the reference explicit. If blue seems to have landed as flirting when you meant friendship, ask directly: friend vibe, but let me know if I read that wrong.

faqs.question: What does 💙 mean from a guy
faqs.answer: When a male friend sends it, 💙 usually means friendship or same-sex friendship without romantic intent. Context still matters, especially if the relationship is new or the conversation is unusually intimate.

faqs.question: Is 💙 flirty
faqs.answer: 💙 can be flirty, but it is also widely used for friendship and team loyalty, so it is not a clear romantic signal by itself. In a dating conversation, spelling out your interest removes the guesswork.

faqs.question: What does 💙 mean on TikTok
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 💙 commonly reacts to a creator, club, or sports team the sender supports. It may also appear between friends as an affectionate sign-off.

faqs.question: What does 💙 mean in a baby announcement
faqs.answer: In the blue-for-boy convention used for gender reveals, 💙 announces that the baby is a boy. In other contexts, the same blue heart means friendship or support for a team.

conversationExamples.message: we both chose the worst movie on purpose 💙
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a friendly sign that the sender recognizes a shared taste and enjoys the connection. Reply with another playful observation; if you want romantic interest to be clear, say that directly.
The heart expresses warm same-sex friendship rather than a romantic confession. A matching 💙 or a simple I love you too will keep the exchange natural.

conversationExamples.message: love where this team is heading 💙
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is expressing team solidarity and appreciation for the project's direction. If approval needs to be formal, follow it with a specific sentence naming what worked well.
Here 💙 is part of a gender reveal and identifies the expected baby as a boy. Congratulate the family and use the baby's name if you already know it.

conversationExamples.message: my team better win this one 💙
conversationExamples.interpretation: The heart marks loyalty to the sender's team and may also carry some excited or sarcastic energy. Reply with the team's name, another heart, or a prediction.
